title: Spike: verify and fix clustering determinism
description:
The Louvain implementation iterates HashMap keys, which have random order in Rust. This likely causes non-deterministic community assignments across identical inputs, triggering reconciliation churn even when nothing changed.

Experiment:
1. Run discover_components twice on the same DB state (or call louvain directly on the same WeightedAdj)
2. Diff community assignments — if they differ, the hypothesis is confirmed
3. Fix: sort node IDs (collect to sorted Vec<i64>) before the main Louvain loop
4. Re-run and verify results are now stable

Key files:
- src/components/clustering.rs: louvain() at line 130 — `adj.keys().copied().collect()` is the non-deterministic line
- src/components/clustering.rs: build_weighted_adjacency() — HashMap output order also non-deterministic

acceptance_criteria.text: Demonstrated whether current clustering is deterministic or not
If non-deterministic: fix landed and verified stable across repeated runs

execution_record: Confirmed the bug: without the fix, insertion order [4, 6, 2, 5, 1, 3] produces flipped community assignments ({4:0,1:1,2:1,6:0,5:0,3:1} vs {3:0,2:0,4:1,6:1,5:1,1:0}). Two-line fix — sort node IDs, add tie-breaking. 546 lib tests pass.
